title: docs(agents): name the compliant sync route in the force-push ban clause
body:
Fixes #5239

## What this changes

One clause in root `AGENTS.md`, §9 多 agent 协作纪律 (line 251) — the force-push ban. One line changed, one line added, nothing else in the diff.

The adopted direction is the filer's **first** shape, graded by the skills seat on all four decision axes: **keep the ban absolute and name the compliant route in the same clause.** The rejected second shape — an "owned branch" exception permitting `--force-with-lease` on single-owner branches — is deliberately **not** implemented here.

## Why

The ban is absolute and names `--force-with-lease` explicitly, but its parenthetical rationale — 「会覆盖并行 agent 的工作」 — is about a **shared** ref. That reason does not obtain on a per-task, single-owner `claude/issue-*` branch, which the worktree-first discipline in this same section guarantees is owned by exactly one agent. A dev syncing its own branch onto current `main` therefore arrives at a step the rules forbid, with no compliant alternative named anywhere in the file. Merging `main` into the branch was presumably the intended answer; it was something each dev had to infer.

The measured instance (a dev's correct, unprompted self-report on PR #5231) is the evidence that a careful dev following the surrounding discipline is routed into the prohibition. Nothing is remediated on that PR — no harm resulted there, and it is not touched by this change. #5177 is not addressed here.

## The edit

The original sentence, its wording and its scope, are carried through **verbatim**; what follows it is new:

- the ban does not grade on whether the branch has a single owner — that judgment has no symptom when evaluated wrongly, and its failure mode is the silent work loss this section exists to prevent;
- the compliant sync route by name: `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main`, resolve, push normally;
- the cost is one merge commit, which does not reach `main` because this repo's PRs land through the queue with `--squash`;
- a closing parenthetical noting that queue merges do **not** require syncing at all (the queue rebuilds on current `main`), so this addition does not contradict the 「不必为了合并去 rebase 其他在途分支」 rule further down the same section. Proactive syncing earns its keep by surfacing a break someone else just landed, ahead of the queue.

Written in Chinese to match the clause and the section around it; machine-relevant tokens (`--force-with-lease`, `git merge origin/main`, `--squash`) stay literal. No stop-sign glyph — that idiom appears zero times in this file today.

## Checks (all run on `0ae747183`, the head of this PR)

| check | verdict line |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | `check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 4682 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `No source of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` |
| `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` | `Links are valid across 13 scan roots.` |

**No changeset**, and this is measured rather than assumed: the presence check — the mechanism `.github/workflows/changeset-presence.yml` enforces — reports `1 file(s) changed, 0 of them under the src/ of a package the release covers`. A root instruction file is not a released package's `src/`, so nothing is owed; the empty-frontmatter declaration form applies to changes that *do* touch released `src/`. `AGENTS.md` is also outside `check-doc-links.mjs`'s scan roots, and this edit adds no links.

## Merge posture

Governed agent-instruction surface. **Draft, maintainer merge only** — do not flip ready, do not enable auto-merge. This must not ride on a code PR, and does not: `AGENTS.md` is the only file in the diff.

Serial constraint re-verified on a fresh fetch at dispatch time: none of the 5 open objectui PRs (#5207, #4958, #4950, #4945, #4655) touches `AGENTS.md`.
